checks.name: clause 1 caveat 2b: 'recall cannot be bought by dropping rules' is FALSE as stated
checks.detail: THE ONE CLAIM THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE. src/rag/deep_research.py:1619-1620 asserts 'The claim that cannot be bought this way is criteria_recall: dropping rules can only ever remove chances to match.' The project's own data falsifies it. deep-r2-admit is deep-r2 with two rules removed and NOTHING else changed — a strict subset — and its recall is HIGHER: 0.3684 -> 0.4211, seven applicable criteria counted -> eight. The mechanism is visible and is not the exclusivity gate: r0401 is grounded with the same exclusive chunk (chunk:fD0E57QYSPk:15) in all four deep arms, so grounding did not change. What changed is the matcher's one-to-one assignment. In deep-r2, c22 was matched to nothing at all; in deep-r1 it was matched to r0602 and discarded as ungrounded; in the two thinned arms it landed on r0401. Fewer candidate findings means less competition for a criterion, so thinning a pack can hand a criterion to a grounded survivor. HOW MUCH THIS MATTERS: the magnitude is inside the noise — deep-r2's own repeat median is 0.4211, the same as admit's point estimate — so this is not evidence that recall WAS bought, and it does not touch deep-frontier's disjointness against merged, which is measured 5/5 against 5/5. But the defence is stated as an impossibility and it is not one. It should read 'dropping rules is not a reliable way to buy recall', not 'cannot'. Recorded as a failed check because it is a claim the build makes in its own source and the data contradicts it; it does not fail clause 1, whose comparison is frontier against merged.

The single criterion frontier counts that admit does not is c18, which is not applicable and therefore scores nothing. So the coverage-aware critic plus frontier retrieval bought ZERO additional applicable criteria over an ablation that costs no LLM call at all. Their only measured difference is repeat stability: admit's floor is 0.3158 and overlaps merged's 0.3684 ceiling; frontier's floor is 0.4211 and does not. That is a real difference and it is the whole of the difference. A reader should understand the pass as 'the pack got more consistently matchable', not 'the pack found more'.

notes: PLAIN ANSWER: this is a PASS. All three clauses now pass. Clause 1 is carried by deep-frontier reaching or beating the hand-built merged pack on all four V3 metrics — criteria_recall 0.421 vs 0.263 with the two arms' five-repeat ranges fully disjoint, evidence_precision 0.875 vs 0.824, provenance tied at 1.000, contested_coverage unscoreable in both — which is the same standard, applied the same way, that failed attempt 1. Two of the builder's supporting claims are false and are recorded as failed checks; neither of them is load-bearing for the clause, and I have said why below rather than letting a pass absorb them.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED, STATED PRECISELY. Attempt 1 failed because the loop's added rules diluted grounding: deep-r2 grew the pack from 16 to 26 rules and evidence_precision fell from 0.813 to 0.769, below the hand build's 0.824. Attempt 2 does not add better rules so much as it stops adding bad ones — 24 rules instead of 26, 21 grounded instead of 20. The single change that does the work is the evidence-novelty admission rule, and the run proves it: deep-r2-admit, which is deep-r2 with that rule and no new LLM call, already reaches 0.4211 / 0.875 and ties deep-frontier on every scored figure and on the exact set of applicable criteria reached. The coverage-aware critic and the frontier retrieval add nothing to the point estimates. What they add is repeat stability — admit's recall floor is 0.3158 and still overlaps merged, frontier's is 0.4211 and does not — and that stability is the entire reason clause 1 passes rather than ties. So the honest one-line summary is: a free filter got the pack over the line on the point estimates, and the two expensive changes got it over the line on the spread.

IS THE 'AGAINST THE HAND BUILD' READOUT FAIR, OR BUILT TO PASS? Fair, on the substance. It applies the rule I applied when I failed deep-r2 — clear the other side's maximum — in its most conservative form, my worst against your best; it fills a gap winner() structurally cannot fill, since winner() compares leader to runner-up and two loop arms tie here; it renders 'ranges overlap' honestly when the ranges cross; and every input is committed data whose arithmetic I reproduced from cell.match_runs without touching the component. What is weak is not the rule but its home: it is a React component computed at render time, absent from the committed run JSON, absent from winner(), and unreachable by the eval harness. Anyone reading evals/runs/critique-15rTnqKBlO8-20260811-025343.json sees only 'tied' on all three scoreable metrics. A pass that exists only in the browser is a weaker artifact than one recorded in the run file, and the fix is small: compute the baseline pair in pack_ablation.py beside winner() and commit it.

THE CLAIM THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE, AND WHY IT DOES NOT SINK THE PASS. src/rag/deep_research.py states that criteria_recall 'cannot be bought this way' because 'dropping rules can only ever remove chances to match'. That is false, and the counterexample is in the same run: deep-r2-admit is a strict subset of deep-r2 — same rules minus two — and scores HIGHER, 0.3684 -> 0.4211, seven applicable criteria -> eight. The mechanism is not the exclusivity gate (r0401 is grounded on the same exclusive chunk in every deep arm) but the matcher's one-to-one assignment: thinning the candidate pool reduces competition for a criterion, and c22 — unmatched in deep-r2, matched to an ungrounded rule in deep-r1 — lands on grounded r0401 in both thinned arms. The magnitude sits inside the matcher noise (deep-r2's own repeat median is already 0.4211), so this is not evidence that recall was bought; it is evidence that the impossibility claim is wrong. It should be restated as 'dropping rules is not a reliable way to buy recall'. It does not sink clause 1 because the clause compares deep-frontier against merged, not against deep-r2, and that comparison is 5/5 repeats disjoint.

THE c22 CLAIM IS WRONG ON BOTH COUNTS, AND IT WAS THE CLAIM MOST WORTH CHECKING. Presented as the strongest evidence if true — deep-frontier the only pack in the project to reach 'aim the document at one clear role persona'. It is not the only pack: deep-r2-admit reaches c22 as well. And neither reaches it through anything the frontier round built. In both arms c22 is matched to r0401, a round-1 rubric that is byte-identical across deep-r1, deep-r2, deep-r2-admit and deep-frontier, that was grounded and available in all of them, and that simply went unmatched in the two unthinned arms. So the correct statement is not 'the loop reached a criterion nothing had reached' but 'thinning the pack let the matcher pair an existing rule with a criterion it had previously left on the floor'. The mitigating fact, and it is a real one: this claim is nowhere in the shipped app. I searched the rendered page for c22, 'persona', 'only pack', 'only arm', 'never reached' and 'no committed arm' and found none. The product does not make the claim; the report to the evaluator did.

WHAT I VERIFIED BY RE-IMPLEMENTATION RATHER THAN BY READING. (a) Every arm's five per-repeat recall scores, rebuilt from cell.match_runs and the dataset's applicable set — all six reported spreads reproduced exactly, so the disjointness claim rests on numbers I derived myself. (b) admit_novel_evidence, re-implemented standalone and run over the shipped packs: merged 0 refused, raptor 3, communities 1, pack 0 — the builder's asymmetry defence is exactly right, and the rule is most lenient on the baseline it competes against. (c) The 261/261 citation figure, summed across arms. (d) deep-frontier's inheritance of deep-r1, compared byte-for-byte. (e) Which applicable criteria each arm counts, and which finding each was matched to — which is how the c22 and admission findings were reached.

THE METRIC'S CEILING STILL APPLIES. src/evals/KNOWN_GAP_attack2.md is now 'partly closed': GATE_PROVENANCE lands option 2, requiring a cited chunk to be one the finding's own reasoning retrieved, and it is applied to all six arms here. But option 1 — an entailment check that the chunk supports the finding attached to it — is still open, so criteria_recall still certifies 'reached the conclusion and cited something that resolves and that it retrieved', not 'the corpus produced this insight'. Weight evidence_precision accordingly, which is what this verdict does: it is the deterministic metric, it failed the slice last time, and it leads now.
